item.title: Lumbar — IASTM
clinicalUse: Use when assessment identifies a relevant impairment in Lumbar and the parent technique fits the patient's presentation.
Primary treatment target: low-back movement, local pain, lower-limb symptom behavior and function such as bending or sit-to-stand.
Retain the technique only if it produces a meaningful within-session improvement.
patientPosition: Prone, side-lying or supine based on the technique and symptom response.
Use abdominal/pelvic support if it reduces irritability.
therapistPosition: Stand close to the trunk with neutral wrists and controlled body weight.
stabilization: Control pelvis and adjacent trunk so the intended manual input is localized.
contact: Use broad lumbar/paraspinal or pelvic contact and avoid direct pressure over painful bony prominences.
Use an appropriate instrument edge over intact skin with lubricant when required by the tool/system.
Keep the tool moving and avoid vulnerable neurovascular structures or bony prominences.
forceDirection: Use light-to-moderate scanning or treatment strokes; excessive redness/bruising is not the goal.
dosage: Often 30–120 seconds per small area within a brief treatment bout, followed by active movement/loading.
steps: 1. Record the exact comparable sign for Lumbar: low-back movement, local pain, lower-limb symptom behavior and function such as bending or sit-to-stand.
2. Screen regional red flags, contraindications and technique-specific precautions before touching the patient.
3. Position and stabilize the patient so the target is comfortable and the manual input can be localized.
4. Apply a low-force trial using the parent technique principles and the region-specific contact described above.
5. Monitor pain quality, symptom distribution, guarding and patient confidence throughout.
6. Re-test the original comparable sign immediately after the trial.
7. Keep the technique only when the response is useful, then transfer the gain into active movement, loading or self-management.
mistakes: Applying the technique because it is familiar rather than because the examination supports it.
Using more force when the response is unclear or worsening.
Failing to re-test the exact movement or function that justified the treatment.
safety: Screen cauda equina features, fracture, infection, malignancy and progressive neurological loss before routine manual treatment.
Stop or modify if symptoms peripheralize, neurological status worsens, the response is disproportionate or the patient asks to stop.
item.visualCue: Lumbar assessment → correct regional setup → IASTM → immediate comparable-sign re-test.

subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve pain, movement tolerance or tissue-related function when this target is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Prone, side-lying or supine with pelvis/trunk supported.
subTechniques.contact: Appropriate instrument edge over intact skin at Quadratus lumborum with conservative pressure.
subTechniques.direction: Use light-to-moderate scanning/treatment strokes; bruising is not the goal.
subTechniques.dosage: Often 30–120 seconds per small area followed by active movement/loading.
subTechniques.reassess: Re-test the region's original pain, range or functional task.
